corpusA.desc: 4 arXiv papers: Transformer, BERT, Sentence-BERT, RAG (11–19 pages each)

corpusB.desc: 2 long arXiv papers: GPT-3 (75 pages) and Llama 2 (77 pages)

notes: Full evidence retrieved: A 7 → 8 of 10, B 2 → 5 of 6 answerable questions
Long documents gain most from a larger top-k
Persistent misses: F3 (wording mismatch) and a cross-document comparison (LM2)
retrieval.speaker: Bars show the share of answerable questions whose full evidence was in the retrieved chunks, judged from the chunk text (final V1.1 runs; A n=10, B n=6). Small samples: one question is 10 to 17 points. F3's evidence ranks 22nd for its wording but 1st when the question says 'Wikipedia dump'.

quality.abstainLabel: unanswerable responses correctly abstained (5 questions × 2 settings)
quality.note: False premises: never corrected; abstained in 5 of 6 responses, fabricated once (A2 at top-k 8). More context did not always help the 3B model.
quality.speaker: Judged outcomes for answerable questions in the final runs. Top-k 8 retrieves more evidence but corpus A correct answers went 7 to 6, latency roughly doubled (7 s to 13 s), and the only hallucination appeared at top-k 8. See docs/evaluation_report.md.

failures.title: F3: RAG's Wikipedia index
failures.what: The evidence on p. 4 ranked 22nd: the question says 'non-parametric memory', the passage says 'Wikipedia dump'.
failures.status: Partly fixed (V1.3): hybrid + rerank now gives Wikipedia and 21M; the p. 4 dump passage is still missed.

failures.title: D1: NIST six Functions
failures.what: Evidence ranked 55th: the running page header made every chunk look alike, and the list was a small part of its chunk.
failures.status: Fixed (V1.3): headers stripped + reranker; now answered correctly.

failures.title: A2: false premise
failures.what: 'Why does SBERT use [CLS] by default?' (it uses MEAN). V1 justified the premise from BERT passages.
failures.status: Fixed: rule 10, then V1.3 retrieval; now says MEAN is the default.

failuresSpeaker: Each failure was root-caused before any change. F3 and D1 were retrieval failures with verified causes, which is what V1.3 targeted. A2 was a hallucination fixed by a prompt rule; with better retrieval the model now corrects the premise. The BLEU table case (prompt rule 9) is in the report.
limitations: No OCR: scanned PDFs are rejected with an explanation
Tables lose structure in extraction (D4: 3 of 4 rows)
3B model misreads some retrieved text (D5, D6, S1)
Single-user local prototype; 33 questions, one run per setting
improvements: Stronger LLM: 16 GB+ machine or the OpenAI-compatible setting (8B tested: better reading)
Premise check before answering (A1, LA1, DA1)
conclusion: A working local RAG chatbot that cites file and page and declines when the answer is not in the PDFs, tested on research papers and a government policy document. Evaluation found retrieval was the bottleneck; hybrid search and a reranker cut wrong answers from 7 to 2 of 22. The next limit is the 3B model's reading.

points: Short papers: MMR worse; drops the chunk that continues a passage
Fixed A2's hallucination at k8; added 2 misattributed numbers
MMR kept as a UI option; V1.3 default is hybrid + rerank
mmr.speaker: V1.2 adds MMR retrieval and makes the LLM parameters explicit. Same 24 questions, same judging rules. MMR fetches 20 candidates and picks 4 or 8 that are relevant but not redundant. It helped on the long GPT-3 and Llama 2 papers and hurt on the short papers, because with 200-character overlap the next chunk of a passage looks redundant to MMR. The context window was measured: Ollama truncates at 4096 tokens by default, and the largest prompt is about 2,500 tokens, so nothing was cut. See evaluation report sections 8b and 8c.

corpusC.desc: Different domain: NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 (government policy, public domain)

points: Fixes target verified causes: running headers stripped; BM25 for exact terms; cross-encoder for buried sentences
Evidence in the top 4: 9 → 16 of 26 questions (retrieval-only test)
All 7 unanswerable questions still declined; +1.5 s per answer
llms: declines most questions with this prompt
reads better, ~4× slower, exceeds 8 GB GPU
v13.speaker: The evaluation showed retrieval misses were the main failure, with two verified causes: wording mismatch and repeated page headers. V1.3 targets exactly those: headers are stripped, BM25 keyword search is merged with embedding search, and a cross-encoder reranks 30 candidates. Retrieval alone: the full evidence reached the top 4 for 16 of 26 questions instead of 9. With the LLM: wrong answers fell from 7 to 2 of 22, correct rose from 11 to 12, and every unanswerable question was still declined. The reranker gave most of the gain; hybrid alone did not help on the NIST document. Top-k 6 was also tested and was not better. LLM comparison with the same retrieval: Qwen 2.5 3B declined most questions with this prompt; Llama 3.1 8B read tables better but was four times slower and overflowed the 8 GB GPU, so Llama 3.2 3B stays. See evaluation report section 8e.
